analysis.title: InView November 2026: Global House View & Investment Perspectives - Navigating equity market rotation
key_insights: MSCI All Country World Index fell more than 1.6% in October, trimming year-to-date gains to just over 11%. A sharp style rotation took place: value sectors gained strongly while growth sectors suffered heavy losses.

A reassessment of AI-related investment, particularly how AI spending affects the cash generating capacity of the large hyperscalers, drove the growth sell-off. MSCI EM fell nearly 9% in USD terms in October versus a 0.7% decline in developed markets, largely due to the US technology sell-off.

Government bond yields fell in the US, Germany, the UK and Switzerland even as inflation remains high and central banks signal further hikes may be necessary. The rally also reflects concerns about public debt in France and other eurozone countries.

The 10-year French-German government bond spread has climbed to levels last seen in 2011. Investors are anxious about French public finances ahead of the 2027 presidential election, where polls currently favour Marine Le Pen.
Gold has retreated to its 2026 lows, extending the correction since late January to more than 30%, despite falling government bond yields, a broadly stable US dollar and geopolitical risks.

House stance: moderate overweight in global equities favouring Japan and the US, slight underweight in fixed income with a little more duration than benchmark. Cash was raised by trimming hedge funds to prepare for buying opportunities if markets turn volatile after the US midterm elections.

Fixed income: above-benchmark duration is maintained after the retreat in yields validated last month's decision to extend. The house prefers investment grade across major currencies, overweights euro and sterling sovereigns, and favours the intermediate part of the yield curve.

Credit: spreads offer limited protection against adverse scenarios. The house is underweight US high yield, EM debt (local and hard currency), hybrids and asset-backed securities, neutral euro high yield and overweight convertibles.

Global allocation: renewed Middle East tensions and elevated energy prices are the main risk. Inflation impact is so far mostly in headline measures, but prolonged energy and transport costs could hit corporate margins and household purchasing power. Alternatives were cut from overweight to neutral and cash raised, though still below neutral.

Equities: earnings expectations are supportive, but valuations in parts of the market are demanding and the bar for positive earnings surprises is high. Technicals are more mixed, with October rotating from higher-beta markets toward defensives and value.

US equities stay overweight, with meaningful small-cap exposure relative to the benchmark even after some reduction last month. Asia ex-Japan stays underweight on technology concentration and volatility.

Within Asia, Taiwan is the preferred market and is being marginally increased on the strongest and broadest bottom-up trends driven by the IT supply chain. Korea was cut from neutral to underweight despite the recent sharp sell-off. Japan, Europe and Latin America outlooks remain constructive.

US sectors: information technology trimmed but still marginally overweight with positive earnings sentiment. Energy and consumer staples raised in line with market drift. Communication services underweight, favouring platform and digital advertising leaders and avoiding traditional telecoms. Utilities stay neutral for now, as bond yields may peak in the coming months but it is too early to add.

Europe sectors: exposure reduced to industrials, financials and technology and raised in consumer staples, healthcare and utilities, citing relative valuation support, earnings visibility and resilience in a late-cycle environment.

UK sectors: industrials are the favoured sector, particularly aerospace and AI capex-linked companies. Financials are the second largest overweight, as the Middle East conflict and energy inflation are expected to produce tighter-for-longer monetary conditions. Consumer staples and real estate are underweight as bond proxies.

Alternatives: hedge fund exposure is reduced but stays overweight, with profits taken. Commodities stay underweight due to energy volatility and precious metals' sensitivity to real yields and the dollar.

Currency: the USD is supported by elevated real yields, resilient activity, energy supply uncertainty, expectations of a restrictive Fed and eurozone debt concerns. The house expects moderate USD depreciation over the medium term as structural headwinds persist and the impact of elevated energy prices fades. The euro has lost ground and the Swiss franc has gained safe-haven status.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong corporate earnings growth, supportive year-end seasonality and possible reduced political uncertainty after the US midterms support risk assets. Broader market leadership could make the advance healthier and more sustainable.
tension_points.bear_case: Valuations in parts of the market are demanding, the hurdle for positive earnings surprises is high, technicals are mixed, and AI spending is being reassessed.
